result.topic_en: Calculations on the zeta function: the completed function $\xi$ and its product over the roots, the Dirichlet series for $\log\zeta(s)$, its integral representation via the prime-counting function $f(x)$, and Fourier/Mellin inversion giving $f(y)$ as a complex line integral.

$\log\xi(s+\frac{1}{2})+\log\Pi(\frac{s}{2}-\frac{3}{4})-\frac{s}{2}\log\pi = \Sigma\log(1+\frac{s^2}{\alpha^2}) + \log\xi(\frac{1}{2}) + \log\Pi(-\frac{3}{4})$ [-...-] [?] ...
$\xi(s)\,\Pi(\frac{s}{2})\,\pi^{-\frac{s}{2}}(s-1)$

$\log\zeta(s) = -\Sigma\log(1-\frac{1}{p^s})$
$= \Sigma p^{-s}+\frac{1}{2}\Sigma p^{-2s}+\frac{1}{3}\Sigma p^{-3s}+\cdots$
$\int_{?}^{\infty} x^{-s}\ldots\,d\log x = \ldots$ [?]
$F(x)$ Anzahl der Primzahlen $< x$
$f(x) = F(x)+\frac{1}{2}F(x^{\frac{1}{2}})+\frac{1}{3}F(x^{\frac{1}{3}})+\cdots$
$\frac{\log\zeta(s)}{s} = \int_0^\infty f(x)\,x^{-s}\,d\log x$
$s=a+bi \Big) = g(b)+h(b)\,i$
$g(b) = \int_0^\infty f(x)\,x^{-a}\cos(b\log x)\,d\log x$
$h(b) = -\int_0^\infty f(x)\,x^{-a}\sin(b\log x)\,d\log x$
$\frac{\pi}{2}f(y)\,y^{-a} = \int_0^\infty g(b)\cos b(\log y)\,db$
$\frac{\pi}{2}f(y)\,y^{-a} = -\int_0^\infty h(b)\sin b(\log y)\,db$
$2\pi i\,f(y) = \int_{a-\infty i}^{a+\infty i}\frac{\log\zeta(s)}{s}\,y^{s}\,ds$

$\frac{\partial\frac{\Sigma\log(1+\frac{(s-\frac{1}{2})^2}{\alpha^2})-\log(s-1)}{s}}{\partial s} = \int_1^\infty x^{-s}\log x\left(Li\,x - \Sigma\left(Li\,x^{\frac{1}{2}+\alpha i}+Li\,x^{\frac{1}{2}-\alpha i}\right)\right)d\log x$
